references.text: Basic legislation concerning the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur), which forbids all work and describes the day as a Sabbath rest for atonement before the Lord.
The Sabbath command to do no work, which forms the basis for the prohibition of labor on the Day of Atonement.
Repeats the prohibition against work on the Day of Atonement and emphasizes that it is an eternal statute.
A parallel passage describing the Day of Atonement with a ban on work and a command to humble oneself.
Describes the annual atonement the high priest was to perform on the altar of atonement, linked to the ritual of the Day of Atonement.
Describes how the high priest entered the Most Holy Place once a year with blood to make atonement for the people's sins, a typological fulfillment of Yom Kippur.
Christ entered the sanctuary with his own blood and secured eternal redemption, fulfilling the meaning of the Day of Atonement.
Explains that the annual sacrifices on the Day of Atonement were a reminder of sin but could not completely take away sins.
God presented Christ as an atoning sacrifice (ἱλαστήριον), fulfilling the purpose of the Day of Atonement to make atonement for the people.
Jesus Christ is the atoning sacrifice (ἱλασμός) for our sins, the ultimate fulfillment of the atonement on the Day of Atonement.
